candidates.exact_span: The known uses of the receiving water(s) Segment 20.6.4.98 are livestock watering, wildlife habitat, marginal warmwater aquatic life and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which designated-use categories apply to the receiving segment determines which numeric water quality criteria—and thus which effluent limits derived from those criteria—are candidates for inclusion in the permit.

candidates.exact_span: The known uses of Segment 20.6.4.99 are warmwater aquatic life, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the applicable use class for this downstream segment affects which criterion sets are invoked in reasonable-potential and water-quality-based limit determinations.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of Animas River, in both Section 20.6.4.403 and 404 NMAC, are coolwater aquatic life, irrigation, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, public water supply, industrial water supply and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The listed designated uses govern which numeric standards (e.g., coolwater vs. warmwater criteria) are compared against effluent for limit derivation; different readings of which reach or segment this applies to would change applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: The limiting pH numeric criteria in 20.6.4.900 NMAC for primary contact and warmwater, marginal warmwater and coolwater aquatic life designated uses are pH within the range of 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (su).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states the numeric pH criterion range that underlies the enforceable effluent limit; a different interpretation of the cited NMAC provision or which use categories bind here would change the applicable limit value for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The site-specific pH standard of 6.6 – 9.0 is established at the end-of-pipe.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the pH limit is measured and enforced at end-of-pipe versus in-stream affects which reported measurement location is compared against the numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The NMIP requires site-specific pH standard to be applied at end-of-pipe for all dischargers.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of NMIP applicability and what constitutes end-of-pipe for this facility determines the sampling point and limit application scope for pH compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: The limitation and monitoring requirements for pH of 6.6 to 9 are continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether pH limits and monitoring carry forward into the current permit term determines if FY2025 measurements are subject to a 6.6–9.0 numeric limit and whether pH monitoring is an enforceable obligation versus report-only or absent.

candidates.exact_span: Federal regulations found at 40 CFR §122.44 (d) state that if a discharge poses the reasonable potential to cause an in-stream excursion above a water quality criterion, the permit must contain an effluent limit for that pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This operative trigger governs whether water-quality-based effluent limits for toxics (beyond technology-based limits) must be included; different readings of the reasonable-potential standard change which pollutants receive numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: The facility is a minor industrial with the highest monthly average flow over the most recent 24-months as 0.177 MGD (0.274 cfs).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Effluent flow (Qe) is an input to reasonable-potential and critical-dilution calculations; a different interpretation of the stated flow value or averaging period would change derived limits for pollutants evaluated under WQBEL procedures.

candidates.exact_span: For industrial facilities, the highest monthly average flow over the most recent 24-months is used for reasonable potential calculations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This specifies the flow statistic and lookback window for reasonable-potential modeling; applying a different flow basis would alter whether reasonable potential is found and thus which numeric limits are imposed.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges to an irrigation ditch. Water only flows in the ditch when the fields need water. The rest of the year the ditch is dry, 4Q3 is 0.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Receiving-water flow (including 4Q3=0) drives critical dilution and reasonable-potential outcomes for Purpose A; intermittent wet/dry conditions affect when discharge-based monitoring is required for Purpose B; documented dry-period semantics bear on how missing results during no-flow intervals are classified for Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: No samples have been taken of the ditch water when flowing and there are no ambient data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Absence of ambient receiving-water data affects whether reasonable-potential and WQBEL limits can be finalized (Purpose A), whether ambient or effluent monitoring waivers apply (Purpose B), and whether missing measurements reflect documented no-data conditions versus unresolved monitoring gaps (Purpose C).

The critical-dilution formula and interpretation of its variables (Qe, F, Qa) directly determine modeled in-stream concentrations and therefore whether effluent limits for evaluated pollutants are derived or omitted.
